source_text: ἐπ' ἐσχάρας, ἣ ἐπὶ τηγάνου, τοῦ ἱερέως τοῦ προσφέροντος αὐτὴν, αὐτοῦ ἔσται. Καὶ πᾶσα θυσία ἀναπεποιημένη ἐν ἐλαίῳ, καὶ μὴ ἀναπεποιημένη, πᾶσι τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἀαρὼν ἔσται· ἑκάστῳ τὸ ἴσον.» Σώζεται καὶ οὗτος ἐν ἐκκλησίαις ὁ νόμος, καὶ βραβεύει τοῖς ἱερουργοῖς τὴν ἰσότητα, διανέμων ἑκάστῳ τῆς ἀναιμάκτου θυσίας ἀπαραλλάκτως τὰ γέρα. Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδὼς ὁ Παῦλος γράφει· «Οὕτω καὶ ὁ Κύριος προσέταξε, τοὺς τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ προσεδρεύοντας, ἐκ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ζῇν.» Καὶ οἱ προσφέροντες τὰς θυσίας, κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου εἰσὶ, καθὰ πάλιν αὐτός πού φησιν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὧδε ἔχει. {ΚΥΡ.} Καταῤῥυθμίζει δὲ αὖ καὶ τῆς αἰνέσεως τὴν θυσίαν, καὶ ὅπως ἂν γένοιτο παρεγγυᾷ, λέγων· «Οὗτος ὁ νόμος θυσίας σωτηρίου, ἣν προσοίσουσι Κυρίῳ· Ἐὰν μὲν περὶ αἰνέσεως προσφέρῃ αὐτὴν, καὶ προσοίσει ἐπὶ τῆς θυσίας τῆς αἰνέσεως, ἄρτους ἓξ σεμιδάλεως ἀναπεποιημένης ἐλαίῳ, καὶ λάγανα ἄζυμα διακεχρισμένα ἐν ἐλαίῳ, καὶ σεμίδαλιν πεφυραμένην ἐν ἐλαίῳ. Ἐπ' ἄρτοις ζυμίταις προσοίσει τὰ δῶρα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ θυσίᾳ αἰνέσεως σωτηρίου· καὶ προσάξει ἓν ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν δώρων αὐτοῦ, ἀφαίρεμα Κυρίῳ. Τῷ ἱερεῖ τῷ προσχέοντι τὸ αἷμα τοῦ σωτηρίου, αὐτῷ ἔσται· καὶ τὰ κρέα θυσίας αἰνέσεως σωτηρίου, αὐτῷ ἔσται. Καὶ ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ δωρεῖται, βρωθήσεται· οὐ καταλείψουσιν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πρωΐ.» Ἐπ' ἄρτοις ζυμίταις τῆς αἰνέσεως τὴν θυσίαν ποιεῖσθαι προστέταχε· καίτοι σαφῶς καὶ ἐναργῶς ἐν ἑτέροις εἰπὼν, ὅτι «Πᾶσαν ζύμην καὶ πᾶν μέλι οὐ προσοίσετε Κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ ὑμῶν. Δῶρον ἀπαρχῆς προσοίσετε αὐτὰ τῷ Κυρίῳ· ἐπὶ δὲ τὸ θυσιαστήριον οὐκ ἀναθήσεται εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ.» Ἆρ' οὖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τὸ περίεργον ἐν τούτοις, οὐκ ὀνησιφόρον εἶναι φής; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Τίς οὖν ἄρα ἔσται τῆς οἰκονομίας ὁ τρόπος, φέρε δὴ λέγωμεν, πολυπραγμονοῦντες ὡς ἔνι, καὶ τρίβον ἱέντες τὴν κεκρυμμένην. Νομικώτατα τοίνυν καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Δαβὶδ τὴν πνευματικὴν ἀνακρούων λύραν, «Ποτήριον,» φησὶ, «σωτηρίου λήψομαι, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου ἐπικαλέσομαι·» τῆς αἰνέσεως τὴν θυσίαν, ποτήριον σωτηρίου διαῤῥήδην ἀποκαλῶν. Προσκομίζομεν δὲ καὶ ἡμεῖς τὴν αἴνεσιν κατὰ πληθὺν μὲν ἐν ἐκκλησίαις, εἰς ἑνότητα πνεύματος, καὶ ὡς εἰς ἓν σῶμα καὶ ψυχὴν μίαν συνενηνεγμένοι διὰ τῆς πίστεως· γέγραπται γὰρ, ὅτι «Τοῦ δὲ πλήθους τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἦν ἡ καρδία καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ μία.» Ποιούμεθα δὲ τὰς δοξολογίας καὶ καθ' ἕνα πολλάκις ἠρεμοῦντες οἶκον, καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ ἐν νυκτί· καὶ τὸ χρῆμά ἐστι τοῖς ἐπιεικέσιν ἐν τριβῇ. Ἢ οὐκ ἀληθὲς ὅ φημι; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς γὰρ οὔ; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλ' εἴτ' οὖν ἐν ἐκκλησίαις κατὰ πληθὺν προσάγοιτο πρὸς ἡμῶν τὸ θῦμα, εἴτ' οὖν ἐν ἑτέροις πράττοιτο τόποις, καὶ καθ' ἕνα τυχὸν, ἢ καὶ κατὰ δύο που, καὶ τρεῖς, καὶ πλείονας ἔτι, ἀδιάκριτος ἡ παράστασις τῶν ὑμνολογεῖν εἰωθότων, καὶ εἰς τοῦτο συνδεδραμηκότων· ὁμοῦ γὰρ τοῖς ἤδη κεκαθαρμένοις διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος, συναναφέρει τὸ θῦμα·
pass_a_gloss: [every one made] on a grate, or on a frying pan, it shall be the priest's who offers it. And every sacrifice mixed up in oil, and not mixed, shall be for all the sons of Aaron; to each the equal.' This law too is preserved in churches, and it awards equality to the ministers, distributing to each without difference the privileges of the bloodless sacrifice. And knowing this Paul writes: 'So also the Lord commanded that those attending the altar live from the altar.' And those offering the sacrifices are sharers of the altar, as again he himself says somewhere. PALL.: So it is. CYR.: And he regulates again also the sacrifice of praise, and charges how it should be done, saying: 'This is the law of the sacrifice of salvation, which they shall offer to the Lord. If he offers it for praise, he shall also offer upon the sacrifice of praise loaves of fine flour mixed up with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and fine flour kneaded in oil. Upon leavened loaves he shall offer his gifts upon the sacrifice of praise of salvation; and he shall bring one from all his gifts, a portion taken off for the Lord. To the priest who pours the blood of the salvation offering, to him it shall be; and the flesh of the sacrifice of praise of salvation shall be his. And on the day on which it is given it shall be eaten; they shall not leave any of it until the morning.' Upon leavened loaves he has commanded the sacrifice of praise to be made; although he said clearly and plainly in other places: 'All leaven and all honey you shall not offer to the Lord your God. As a gift of firstfruits you shall offer them to the Lord; but on the altar it shall not be put up for an odour of fragrance to the Lord.' Do you say then, Palladius, that close inquiry in these things is not profitable? PALL.: Very much so. CYR.: What then will be the manner of the arrangement, come, let us say, searching as far as possible and opening the hidden path. Most in keeping with the law, then, the inspired David too, striking up the spiritual lyre, says: 'I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord,' expressly calling the sacrifice of praise a cup of salvation. And we too bring the praise in multitude in churches, into unity of spirit, and as into one body and one soul brought together through faith; for it is written: 'And of the multitude of those who believed the heart and the soul was one.' And we make the doxologies also often one by one, being quiet in the house, both by day and by night; and the thing is in practice among the upright. Or is what I say not true? PALL.: How not? CYR.: But whether the offering is brought by us in multitude in churches, or is done in other places, perhaps one by one, or two by two somewhere, and three, and still more, the presence of those accustomed to sing hymns and who have run together for this is without distinction; for together with those already cleansed through holy baptism there joins in bringing up the offering
pass_b_english: Cyril: …on a grill or in a pan shall belong to the priest who offers it. And every sacrifice mixed with oil, and every one not mixed, shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, to each an equal share’ (Leviticus 7:9–10). This law too is preserved in the churches, and it secures equality for those who serve at the altar, giving each, without variation, his portion of the bloodless sacrifice. Knowing this, Paul writes: ‘So also the Lord commanded that those who attend the altar should live from the altar’ (1 Corinthians 9:13–14). And those who offer the sacrifices are sharers in the altar, as he himself says again somewhere (1 Corinthians 10:18).

Cyril: He also regulates the sacrifice of praise and directs how it is to be done, saying: ‘This is the law of the sacrifice of salvation that they shall offer to the Lord. If he offers it for praise, then with the sacrifice of praise he shall offer loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour kneaded with oil. With loaves of leavened bread he shall offer his gifts, along with the sacrifice of salvation offered in praise. And he shall bring one out of all his gifts as a portion set apart for the Lord; it shall belong to the priest who pours out the blood of the sacrifice of salvation. And the meat of the sacrifice of salvation offered in praise shall be his, and it shall be eaten on the day it is offered; they shall not leave any of it until morning’ (Leviticus 7:11–15). He has commanded that the sacrifice of praise be made with leavened loaves, even though elsewhere he said clearly and plainly: ‘You shall offer no leaven and no honey to the Lord your God. You shall offer them to the Lord as a gift of firstfruits, but they shall not be put on the altar for a fragrant aroma to the Lord’ (Leviticus 2:11–12). Would you not say, then, Palladius, that looking closely into these things brings profit?

Cyril: What, then, is the meaning of this arrangement? Come, let us say, searching it out as far as we can and opening up the hidden path. So, very much in keeping with the law, the inspired David too, striking up the spiritual lyre, says: ‘I will take the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord’ (Psalm 116:13), and so expressly calls the sacrifice of praise a cup of salvation. And we too offer praise in great numbers in the churches, in unity of spirit, brought together through faith as into one body (Ephesians 4:3–4) and one soul. For it is written: ‘The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and soul’ (Acts 4:32). We also often give glory alone, quietly at home, by day and by night; and this is the habit of good people. Or is what I say not true?
Palladius: How could it not be?

Cyril: But whether the offering is brought by us in the churches in great numbers, or is performed in other places, perhaps by one alone, or by two somewhere, or three, or more still, no distinction is drawn among those present who are accustomed to sing hymns and have gathered for this. For together with those already cleansed through holy baptism there joins in offering the sacrifice…

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-quotation (Leviticus 7:8-10, begun at the end of §26). Ends mid-sentence: the subject of 'συναναφέρει' is 'ὁ κατηχούμενος' (the catechumen) at the head of §28, so the English breaks at 'there joins in offering the sacrifice…'. LXX Leviticus 7:10 reads 'mixed with oil and not mixed' where the Hebrew has 'mixed with oil or dry'; the LXX wording is kept. In Leviticus 7:12 the Migne text prints 'ἄρτους ἓξ σεμιδάλεως' ('six loaves'); the LXX reads 'ἄρτους ἐκ σεμιδάλεως' ('loaves of fine flour') and 'ἓξ' is almost certainly a misprint, so 'loaves of fine flour' is translated. 'θυσία σωτηρίου' is the LXX term for the peace offering; rendered 'sacrifice of salvation' because Cyril's argument links it to the 'cup of salvation' (ποτήριον σωτηρίου). Paul's words are a conflation of 1 Corinthians 9:13 and 9:14 (the Lord commanded those who proclaim the gospel to live by the gospel), so both verses are cited. 'κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου' matches 1 Corinthians 10:18. Cyril's Leviticus 2:11-12 quotation is loose against the LXX. Psalm 116:13 in English numbering = LXX Psalm 115:4. 'εἰς ἑνότητα πνεύματος… ἓν σῶμα' echoes Ephesians 4:3-4 (unity of the Spirit, one body); cited as a clear allusion, but Cyril writes 'one body and one soul', blending it with Acts 4:32; lower-case 'spirit' kept because the phrase here stresses the believers' concord. 'κατὰ δύο… καὶ τρεῖς' may echo Matthew 18:20 (two or three gathered) but the wording is not close; uncited. 'Ἆρ' οὖν… οὐκ ὀνησιφόρον εἶναι φής' is a question expecting assent, rendered positively ('Would you not say… is meant for our profit?') so that Palladius's 'Very much so' keeps its sense. Reviewer: 'τὸ περίεργον ἐν τούτοις' taken as close inquiry into these things (the activity Cyril at once resumes with 'πολυπραγμονοῦντες'), not as 'the curious point'; either reading leaves Palladius's assent intact.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [continuing Lev 7:9-10:] made ἐπ' ἐσχάρας (on a grill) or ἐπὶ τηγάνου (on a pan) shall be the priest's who offers it; every θυσία ἀναπεποιημένη ἐν ἐλαίῳ (mixed with oil) and μὴ ἀναπεποιημένη shall be for all the υἱοὶ Ἀαρών, ἑκάστῳ τὸ ἴσον (to each the equal). This νόμος σώζεται ἐν ἐκκλησίαις and βραβεύει (awards, secures) ἰσότης for the ἱερουργοί, διανέμων (distributing) to each ἀπαραλλάκτως (without variation) the γέρα (portions) of the ἀναίμακτος θυσία (bloodless sacrifice). Knowing this Paul writes: 'So the Κύριος προσέταξε that those προσεδρεύοντας (attending) the θυσιαστήριον live ἐκ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.' And those offering the sacrifices are κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, as he says again somewhere. PALL.: Ὧδε ἔχει. CYR.: He καταρρυθμίζει (regulates) the θυσία τῆς αἰνέσεως (sacrifice of praise) and παρεγγυᾷ (directs) how: Lev 7:11-15: law of the θυσία σωτηρίου (sacrifice of salvation = peace offering); if offered περὶ αἰνέσεως, with the sacrifice of praise ἄρτους [ἓξ, read ἐκ] σεμιδάλεως (loaves of fine flour) ἀναπεποιημένης ἐλαίῳ, λάγανα ἄζυμα διακεχρισμένα (unleavened wafers anointed) with oil, σεμίδαλις πεφυραμένη (kneaded) with oil; ἐπ' ἄρτοις ζυμίταις (on leavened loaves) he offers his δῶρα with the sacrifice of praise of salvation; one from all his gifts as ἀφαίρεμα (portion lifted off) to the Lord; to the priest who προσχέων (pours) the blood of the σωτήριον it shall be; the κρέα his; eaten on the day δωρεῖται (it is given); not left εἰς τὸ πρωΐ. He προστέταχε the sacrifice of praise on leavened loaves, καίτοι (although) σαφῶς καὶ ἐναργῶς elsewhere: 'πᾶσαν ζύμην καὶ πᾶν μέλι οὐ προσοίσετε to the Lord your God; as δῶρον ἀπαρχῆς (gift of firstfruits) offer them to the Lord; but on the altar οὐκ ἀναθήσεται εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας.' Ἆρ' οὖν (expecting yes) τὸ περίεργον (the curious, odd point) in these, οὐκ ὀνησιφόρον (not profit-bearing) do you say? PALL.: Καὶ μάλα. CYR.: What is ὁ τρόπος τῆς οἰκονομίας? Let us say, πολυπραγμονοῦντες (inquiring) ὡς ἔνι (as possible) and τρίβον ἱέντες τὴν κεκρυμμένην (opening the hidden path). Νομικώτατα (most lawfully, very much in keeping with the law) the θεσπέσιος (divine) David, ἀνακρούων (striking up) the πνευματική λύρα: 'ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι, and call on the ὄνομα Κυρίου', διαρρήδην (expressly) calling the θυσία τῆς αἰνέσεως a cup of salvation. We too προσκομίζομεν αἴνεσιν κατὰ πληθύν (in a multitude) in churches, εἰς ἑνότητα πνεύματος, συνενηνεγμένοι (brought together) as into ἓν σῶμα καὶ ψυχὴ μία through πίστις; written: 'of the πλῆθος τῶν πεπιστευκότων the καρδία and ψυχή was μία.' We make δοξολογίαι also καθ' ἕνα (one by one, alone) often ἠρεμοῦντες (keeping quiet) in a house, by day and night; τὸ χρῆμα is ἐν τριβῇ (habitual) for τοῖς ἐπιεικέσιν (the good, reasonable). Or is it not true? PALL.: Πῶς γὰρ οὔ; CYR.: Whether τὸ θῦμα is προσάγοιτο by us in churches κατὰ πληθύν, or done in other places, perhaps by one, or by two, three, more, ἀδιάκριτος (undistinguished) is the παράστασις (standing-by, presence) of those wont ὑμνολογεῖν and συνδεδραμηκότων (who have run together) for this; for ὁμοῦ (together) with those κεκαθαρμένοι through ἅγιον βάπτισμα, συναναφέρει (joins in offering up) τὸ θῦμα [subject in §28: ὁ κατηχούμενος]…
